title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, Compliance Evidence & Risk Exceptions
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standards and operational procedures for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident-response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk & exceptions process. It is intended for engineers, security reviewers, product owners, and compliance stakeholders.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-managed control plane services, hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated control-plane components, and Private deployment reference artifacts under Redwood operational control.
- Excludes third-party SaaS where customers manage their own data residency requirements unless explicitly integrated via Redwood Private connectors.

Owner and contacts
- Primary owner: Security (sec-owners@redwood.example)
- Secondary owners: Eng SRE (sre-owners@redwood.example), Eng Platform (platform-owners@redwood.example)
- On-call (for security ops): sec-oncall (PagerDuty)

1) RBAC and Authentication

Principles
- Least privilege by default; roles grant minimum permissions required for a task.
- Role-based access with groups mapped to corporate SSO (Okta).
- Separation of duties between deploy, operations, and audit functions.
- Short-lived credentials for humans and automated credentials for services with strict rotation.

Role catalog (summary)
- security-admin: Full access to security controls, audit logs, evidence artifacts (restricted).
- platform-operator: Deploy & runtime configuration access for control plane services.
- infra-admin: Fleet and cloud account administration (limited to infra projects).
- svc-account-<service>: Scoped service account for each backend service (no console access).
- read-only-telemetry: Read-only access to metrics, dashboards, and logs for on-call and analytics.

Onboarding / Offboarding checklist
1. Request raised in Access Request system (Jira ticket template: ACCESS-REQ).
2. Owner approves; SSO group assignment applied (Okta SCIM sync).
3. Automated validation: access-review job runs daily to confirm membership.
4. Offboarding: immediate removal from SSO groups, revoke sessions, rotate affected service keys.

Service account best practices
- All service accounts must be named with prefix svc-account- and include owner/team tag.
- Keys are not permitted to be long-lived. Use workload identity or short-lived tokens (e.g., AWS STS/GCP Workload Identity).
- Audit entry required for creation/deletion with justification and reviewer.

RBAC enforcement architecture
- Primary enforcement via IAM for cloud resources + internal policy engine for application-level permissions.
- Policy-as-code repository: repo: infra/policy (PR required for changes; CI enforces tests and linting).

2) Audit Logging

Goals
- Ensure a tamper-evident, queryable record of access and configuration changes across control plane and customer-impacting operations.
- Meet retention SLAs required by customers and compliance frameworks.

Events to capture (minimum)
- Authentication events: login, logout, token issuance, token refresh, MFA events.
- Authorization events: RBAC decision logs, permission changes, role assignments.
- Administrative actions: create/delete/update of service accounts, infrastructure changes, model pin/rollout actions.
- Data access events: datasets read/write/export, embedding exports, audit resource downloads.
- Deployment & config changes: image rollouts, canary promotions, autoscaling policy changes.
- Security events: failed logins, suspicious IPs, MFA bypass attempts, secrets access.

Audit log schema (example fields)
| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| timestamp | UTC ISO8601 | 2027-11-20T15:22:31Z |
| event_id | UUID | 6f1e3a7c-... |
| principal_type | user|service|system | user |
| principal_id | SSO user id / service account id | 0oa1A... |
| action | human-readable action | model.rollout.promote |
| resource_type | service/model/dataset/secret | model |
| resource_id | unique resource identifier | model:open-12b:v2 |
| outcome | success|failure|error | success |
| request_ip | source IP | 18.205.1.2 |
| request_headers | redacted headers | {"user-agent": "curl/7.64"} |
| change_summary | concise change description | promoted canary to 20% |

Log ingestion and storage
- Control plane: centralized logging pipeline (Filebeat -> Kafka -> Log-indexer -> S3 cold storage + Elasticsearch for hot queries).
- Audit logs are append-only in the hot store and immutability markers retained in cold storage.
- Integrity: periodic hash-chaining snapshots stored in write-once storage (S3 Object Lock) for compliance audits.

Availability / SLOs
- Ingestion availability: 99.9% monthly.
- Query latency (hot store): 95th percentile < 1s for 30-day window.

Retention & retention tiers
- Default (hosted customers): audit logs retained 365 days in hot store, archived to cold storage thereafter for an additional 4 years (total 5 years).
- Enterprise regulated customers (contractual): configurable retention up to 7 years.
- Private deployments: retention configurable by customer; Redwood provides recommended defaults and scripts to enable immutability.

Access controls for logs
- Only security-admin and designated auditors have access to raw audit logs. Other teams use RBAC-scoped query views or redacted streams.
- Access is logged and requires an access justification ticket; time-bounded access is encouraged.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Data classification and residency model
- Classified data tiers: public, internal, confidential, regulated.
- Residency options supported: multi-region (US, EU, APAC), single-region, and customer-managed (Private).
- Default for hosted customers: data stored in region selected at account creation; cross-region replication only with explicit customer consent.

Retention policy (summary)
- Metadata and telemetry: 1 year (hot), 4 years archive.
- Customer non-sensitive artifacts (model metadata): 3 years.
- Regulated customer PII or contractual artifacts: per-contract, typical options 7 years.
- Embeddings and user-provided inputs: default 30 days (redwood default), configurable to 0 days (no retention) or longer by enterprise contract.

Data deletion / erasure procedure
1. Customer or internal request submitted via Data Subject Request (DSR) ticket.
2. Validate identity and scope of request.
3. Execute deletion workflow: mark records for deletion -> background job removes from primary DB -> purge from caches (KV) -> schedule cold storage purge (S3 Lifecycle) -> verify with audit log entry.
4. Provide attestation to customer (ticket closure with audit log link).

Cross-region replication & legal considerations
- By default customer data is not replicated outside the chosen residency region. Exceptions require legal review and explicit customer opt-in.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers must declare residency policy during onboarding.

4) Secure SDLC (secure software development lifecycle)

Controls & gates
- Pre-merge checks: automated unit tests, dependency vulnerability scan (Snyk), secrets scanner (TruffleHog / GitHub Advanced Security), linting, and policy-as-code checks.
- Merge requirements: at least one code review by peer + one approval from security for changes touching infra/policy or data handling paths.
- CI/CD pipeline: builds are reproducible, container images scanned and signed (cosign), provenance recorded.
- Environment separation: dev -> staging -> prod with gated approvals for prod promotion.

Security tooling & automation
- SAST: periodic scans for services, scheduled weekly for critical repos.
- Dependency policy: block direct usage of known-vulnerable versions; PRs opened automatically for patches.
- Secrets management: use central secrets backend (AWS Secrets Manager / HashiCorp Vault) and forbid secrets in code with pre-commit guards.

Release checklist (example)
1. All pipeline tests pass and image is signed.
2. Security scan results within thresholds (no critical findings).
3. Canaries configured and rollback plan documented.
4. Owner (eng + product) signs release ticket.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Purpose
- Provide a reproducible, compliance-ready workflow for security incidents that could impact customer data, service availability, or regulatory obligations.

Triage & severity classification
- Sev1 (Critical): confirmed compromise of customer data, active exfiltration, or mass service degradation.
- Sev2 (High): elevated privilege misuse, suspected targeted attack, or customer-impacting security bug.
- Sev3 (Medium): suspicious activity with limited scope.
- Sev4 (Low): informational or potential false positives.

First responder checklist (initial 15 minutes)
1. Acknowledge alert in incident system and notify sec-oncall.
2. Capture volatile evidence (memory snapshots, current process list) when safe and legal.
3. Take containment actions: isolate affected nodes/pods, revoke compromised keys, block suspected IPs at edge.
4. Record all steps in incident timeline (immutable entries preferred).

Forensic evidence collection
- Canonical evidence store: dedicated S3 bucket with Object Lock + access logging.
- Documented collection commands and scripts (example):
  - kubectl: kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o yaml > /tmp/pods-<ts>.yaml
  - capture logs: kubectl logs <pod> --since=2h > /tmp/logs-<pod>-<ts>.log
  - image list: gcloud container images list --repository=gcr.io/redwood | tee /tmp/images-<ts>.txt
- Preserve chain of custody: log who collected what, when, and justification.

Communication & regulatory notifications
- Internal comms: Severity-based notification templates (Slack/PagerDuty + Incident Bridge).
- Customer notification: follow contractual SLA timelines (e.g., notify within 72 hours for confirmed data breach where required by law). Legal must approve external statements.

Post-incident activities
1. Postmortem published within 7 business days for Sev1/Sev2 incidents; include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and preventive actions.
2. Update policy-as-code or runbooks if gaps are found.
3. Evidence retention: incident artifacts kept per compliance retention policy and flagged to auditors.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence types
- Configurations: IaC manifests, environment configs, firewall rules.
- Logs: audit logs, access logs, change history.
- Screenshots/exports: IAM role mappings, policy versions.
- Reports: vulnerability scan outputs, penetration test reports, SOC2 artifacts.

Automated evidence collection
- CI job: nightly evidence snapshot job that exports critical configs and metadata to evidence store.
- Map evidence to control IDs: automated mapping between evidence items and framework controls (SOC2 / ISO27001).

Evidence review and attestations
- Quarterly attestations: control owners must sign attestations for assigned controls (workflow via Confluence+Jira).
- Audit prep runbook: steps to collect, package, and transmit evidence to auditors (including checksums and provenance).

On-demand auditor access
- Read-only, time-bounded access to artifacts via secure temporary roles; all access logged and subject to legal review.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception request process
1. Submit Exception Request (Jira template: RISK-EXC) with: description, risk assessment, compensating controls, duration, and owner.
2. Security reviews request and assigns risk score (Low/Medium/High/Critical).
3. Risk committee approval required for High/Critical (monthly review meeting).
4. Approved exceptions have a maximum timebox (default 90 days) and must include remediation milestones.

Compensating controls examples
- If an S3 bucket cannot be encrypted at rest due to legacy constraints, compensating controls may include network isolation, strict IAM policy, and additional monitoring/alerting.

Tracking and renewal
- All exceptions tracked in the Risk Exceptions register; automated reminders 30/14/3 days prior to expiry. Renewal requires re-evaluation and owner justification.

Appendices

A. Example Jira templates
- ACCESS-REQ (Access Request): fields: requester, owner-team, justification, roles-needed, expiry-date.
- RISK-EXC (Risk Exception): fields: component, description, compensating-controls, expected-remediation-date, approvers.

B. Example CLI snippets
- Export recent audit logs to S3 (one-off):
  aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/redwood/control-plane/audit" --start-time 1609459200000 --end-time 1609545600000 --filter-pattern "model.rollout" | gzip > /tmp/audit-2027-01-01.json.gz
  aws s3 cp /tmp/audit-2027-01-01.json.gz s3://redwood-evidence-bucket/2027/01/01/

C. References
- Security controlbook and integrated playbook (see related pages).
- SOC2 control matrix (internal link provided to auditors).
- Infra/policy repo (git: git@github.com:redwood/infra-policy).
